message.content: Handlers in this codebase return a mode/data reply hash instead of a bare status string because the response payload requires structured metadata beyond a simple success/failure indicator. A status string alone cannot convey which operational mode was entered (e.g., `:boot`, `:idle`, `:fail`), what data was returned, or additional contextual information needed by downstream components. By encapsulating the status, mode, and data within a single hash, the protocol enforces a consistent response schema that allows callers to reliably parse and route responses without relying on string parsing or heuristic matching. This design also future-proofs the API—if new response fields need to be added (e.g., timestamps, metadata, or sub-errors), they can be appended to the hash without breaking existing consumers, whereas a bare status string would require versioning or fragile string-matching logic to interpret.
